A familiar moment
Every day, a child runs into
a word they don't understand.
And most of the time, they just move on, hoping it wasn't important.
But then…
One word left unclear,
and the whole sentence breaks.
Understanding stops. Confidence cracks. And the child learns that "I don't get it" is a place too comfortable to stop.
1 The problem
The old dictionary gives
one dry definition.
One meaning out of many, with no living example, no context, no story. A line you can't hold on to.
The result
The word doesn't stick.
And by tomorrow, it's forgotten.
Without deep understanding and repetition, every search starts from zero. Vocabulary never grows.
The usual fixes
Google and search give an answer,
but don't build understanding.
  • A wall of text that a child won't really read, and not at their level.
  • In the wrong language not the language the child thinks in.
  • Forgotten by tomorrow no notebook, no review, no habit.
